That sounds really intense and scary. How are you feeling about the panic attack?
Pretty shaken, to be honest. It was like everything was closing in on me. I felt so out of control.
It must have been a frightening experience. It's important to acknowledge those feelings. Have you had panic attacks before?
Not like this. I've felt stressed, but this was different. My heart was racing, and I couldn't breathe properly.
Experiencing that for the first time can be very unsettling. How have you been managing at work since then?
I've been trying to keep up, but I'm worried it might happen again. It's hard to focus sometimes.
I understand. The worry of it happening again can add to your stress. Have you considered talking to someone at work about your workload?
I've thought about it, but I'm unsure how to approach it. I don't want to seem incapable.
It's perfectly okay to seek support or ask for help. Everyone has limits. Perhaps there's a way to address the workload without compromising your position.
Maybe I should try setting some boundaries. It's just hard to navigate sometimes.
That's a good idea. Setting boundaries can help manage stress. Have you considered any strategies for handling stress outside of work?
Not really. I think I need to find a way to relax more and maybe pick up a hobby.
Finding something you enjoy could really help. Sometimes stepping away and doing something we love can reset our mind.
You're right. I think I'll start looking for something new to do in my free time. Thanks for listening.
I'm glad to hear that. Remember, I'm here if you need to talk more or if you just need someone to listen. You're doing great, Charlotte.
Hey Charlotte, how have things been going lately?
Hi...it's been a rough couple of days. I had a pretty stressful event at work.
I'm really sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about what happened?
Well, I found some errors in the project report I submitted, and my boss called me out in front of everyone. It was humiliating.
That sounds incredibly stressful, especially since you've been dealing with a lot of pressure at work already.
Yes, exactly. It's like everything is piling on top of me, and I can't seem to catch a break.
It makes sense that you'd feel overwhelmed. Are there any parts of the project or your workload that are more manageable for you?
I guess there are some smaller tasks I can focus on, but even those feel daunting right now.
I understand. It might help to break them down into even smaller steps, to make them feel a bit more doable.
I've thought about that, but it's hard to start when I'm just so exhausted all the time.
I remember you mentioned issues with sleep in the past and how that's been affecting your energy levels.
Yeah. It’s been a persistent problem, and the stress from work only makes it harder to manage.
That sounds really tough, especially since it’s a cycle that feeds into itself. Are there any strategies you’ve tried that have helped even a little?
I tried meditation and some breathing exercises which were somewhat helpful before. But I haven't been consistent with them.
It might be worth giving those another shot when you have a moment to yourself. Even small doses of relief can add up.
You're right. I should try to make it a routine instead of just something I turn to when things get really bad.
That sounds like a great start. Making a little time every day for yourself could help ease some of that pressure.
Thanks for listening. It means a lot to have someone to talk to who understands what I'm going through.
Anytime, Charlotte. You're doing your best under really tough circumstances, and I'm here whenever you need to talk.
Thank you. I think I'll try setting up a time every day to meditate and maybe even talk to someone at work about easing my workload.
That sounds like a solid plan. Taking those steps could make a big difference. And remember, it's okay to seek help; you're not alone.
I will. Thanks again for being there and for your support.
Of course, Charlotte. I'm always here to listen and support you.
Hi! I really need to talk to someone about something that's been weighing on me.
Of course, Charlotte. I'm here to listen. What's going on?
Work has been really tough lately, and my hours have increased without any official notice. It's adding so much stress.
That sounds incredibly frustrating and exhausting. It must be hard to handle those kinds of expectations without any formal agreement.
It really is. I feel like there's just no end in sight, especially after everything that happened last month.
I remember you mentioning how stressed you were after that public criticism from your boss. It seems like things haven't let up for you since then.
Exactly. I thought things might get better, but it feels like I'm just being given more and more to handle.
It's incredibly tough to manage when the workload keeps increasing. Have you had a chance to bring this up with your manager yet?
I've been thinking about it, but I'm afraid it'll make things worse or that I'll be seen as incapable.
That's a valid concern, but remember, asking for what you need doesn't make you weak. It's important to advocate for yourself.
I know you're right, but every time I think about it, my anxiety flares up. It's like I'm trapped in this cycle.

It's understandable considering your past experiences with panic and stress at work. Maybe you could start by writing down your thoughts before you approach the conversation. It might help ease some anxiety.
That could be a good idea. Organizing my thoughts might give me the confidence to bring up the conversation.
Absolutely. Plus, it might help you feel more in control and prepared. Sometimes a little structure can make a big difference.
I'll try that. I just wish I could find a way to manage all of this stress better.
It's definitely not easy, especially with your ongoing sleep issues. Have you been able to take any steps for self-care recently?
Not as much as I'd like. It's just so overwhelming right now, but I know I need to prioritize it more.
Self-care often falls to the wayside when things get tough, but it's crucial. Even small steps, like a daily walk or setting a bedtime routine, can be beneficial.
Maybe I can start with that. Create a small routine that grounds me a bit each day.
That sounds like a positive step, Charlotte. Remember, it's about finding balance and small adjustments can have a big impact.
Thank you for being there and listening. It means so much to know I'm not in this alone.
You're never alone. I'm here for you. Feel free to reach out anytime you need to talk or share.
I will. Just having this conversation has already lightened the load a bit.
I'm really glad to hear that. Keep taking it one day at a time. You've got this.
One day at a time. I'll remember that. Thanks again.
Hey, I really need someone to talk to right now.
Of course, Charlotte. What's on your mind?
I just had a falling out with one of my closest friends. She said I've been distant lately.
I'm sorry to hear that. It must be so hard to hear those words from a friend.
Yeah, it really hurt. I didn't even realize I was being distant.
It sounds like you're dealing with a lot on your plate. Sometimes, things just pile up and we don't even realize how it's affecting those around us.
Exactly. Work has been a mess lately. I feel like I'm drowning, and now this with my friend... it's just too much.

With all that's happened at work, it's understandable you might feel overwhelmed. Remember how you handled the panic attack at work the last time? It can feel like there's no way out, but you managed then.
I remember. It took a lot out of me to get through that period, though. Now with the added stress of this disagreement... I don't know what to do.
It's completely normal to feel this way. You've been managing a lot between the work stress, the criticism from your boss, and now these long hours.
I just feel like I can't catch my breath. Every time I think things are getting better, something else happens.
I'm really sorry you're feeling this way, Charlotte. It's important to acknowledge how you're feeling and give yourself some grace.
Thanks. I think I need to find a way to communicate with my friend and maybe even try and talk to my boss about cutting back my hours.
That sounds like a good plan. Communication can sometimes be that bridge to understanding. Approaching your friend with openness might bring clarity.
I hope so. I'm just worried that she'll be too hurt or that I'll mess things up with my boss.
It's okay to feel worried, but acknowledging how you feel is the first step. When you reach out, it can help to be genuine and share how overwhelmed life's been for you.
Right. I guess honesty would be best. I've been avoiding it because I'm scared of saying the wrong thing.
That's totally understandable. Remember, you're human and it's okay to feel vulnerable at times. Trying to be honest with yourself and them might help.
Thanks for listening. I didn't realize how much I needed this talk.
Anytime, Charlotte. You're not alone in this, and I'm here whenever you need to chat or just vent.
I appreciate it more than you know. I'll try to take it a step at a time.
Exactly, small steps are key. Take care of yourself and remember, progress is still progress, no matter the pace.
Hey Charlotte, I saw your message. How are you holding up today?
Hi, it's been a tough day again. I had another disagreement at work with a coworker.
I'm sorry to hear that. What happened with your coworker?
We got into it because they felt I wasn't contributing enough to the team.
That sounds really frustrating, especially with everything you've been dealing with lately.
It just hit me hard. I’ve been putting in extra hours and still feel like it’s never enough.
That makes sense, considering you've had your work hours extended unofficially. That's a lot of pressure.
Exactly. And it's starting to take a toll on me, both physically and mentally.
It's completely understandable to feel that way. Are you managing to get any rest?
Not really. My sleep's been all over the place, and I can't seem to shake off this constant stress.
Lack of sleep can definitely amplify stress. Have you tried any methods to relax before bed?
I used to try meditation, but I just don’t have the energy these days.
Even small moments of self-care can sometimes help, though I can imagine it feels overwhelming to think about.
Yeah, it's hard to even think about self-care right now, with so much going on.
Maybe it would help to take a step back and acknowledge how much you're managing to do despite everything.
It's just hard when it feels like all eyes are on me, waiting for me to mess up.
It's understandable to feel that pressure. People often only see the surface, not all the hard work you're putting in.
That's true. I have been trying really hard, just wish it was recognized more.
It's important to recognize it for yourself, too. You’ve been through a lot and are still pushing forward.
Thanks for saying that. It means a lot to hear someone understands.
Of course, Charlotte. You’re doing the best you can, and that's something to be proud of.
I need to keep reminding myself of that. Thanks for listening. It’s really helped.
Anytime. Feel free to reach out anytime you need to talk or just need a break.
I will. Thanks again for being there.
Take care, Charlotte. You've got this.
Hey Charlotte, how have you been holding up recently?

Social events can be overwhelming, especially if there's a lot going on. What was the gathering about?
It was supposed to be just a casual meet-up, but there were a lot of potential networking opportunities. It felt really high-stakes for me.
That does sound intense. How did you feel being in that environment?
I was really anxious at first. I've been feeling a lot of pressure at work lately, and it just sort of carried over.
Considering everything that's been happening at work, it's understandable to feel that way. How did you manage your anxiety while you were there?
I tried to focus on engaging one-on-one, which helped a bit, but it was hard to shake the feeling of being judged or not doing enough.
That's a smart strategy, reaching out in smaller settings. It's important to remember that these situations aren't always about being perfect, just about making connections.
Yeah, I guess I keep remembering the times my boss publicly criticized me for inaccuracies. It's like I'm scared of making a mistake again, but now in any setting.
That experience left a big impact on you. It's understandable to be cautious, but networking is really more about building relationships than being flawless.
I know you're right. I did meet a couple of interesting people, and a friend there was really supportive. It was nice to not feel so stuck in my head for once.
That's so great to hear! Having support, especially from friends, can make such a difference in these moments. How did the evening wrap up for you?
Actually, by the end of the night, I felt a bit more relaxed. We ended up talking and laughing about random things. It was a nice distraction from work issues.
It sounds like you found some brightness in those connections despite the initial stress. Do you feel like you could attend more events like this in the future?
I think I could. This experience taught me that not everything has to revolve around job performance. It's okay to just enjoy the moment.
Exactly, sometimes it's the small joys that help us regain balance. Have you thought about discussing these experiences with your therapist?
I might bring it up. Therapy's been a space where I can talk candidly about my work stress. Talking about the better moments could be helpful too.
That sounds like a great plan. Remember, progress isn't always linear, but acknowledging the positive steps is just as important.
Thanks, I agree. I'll try to hold onto these good moments as I move forward.

Of course, Charlotte. I'm here for you. What's been happening?

That sounds exciting, meeting someone new can bring fresh perspectives. But it's also understandable to feel stress, especially after everything you've experienced.

Those were significant challenges. And I remember your workload and social conflicts taking a toll on you. How are you managing those feeling now?

It sounds like you're carrying a lot. Finding a new connection can be refreshing, but it's okay to still feel burdened by past stress. Have you been able to talk about this with your therapist, though?

Taking it slowly is important. It's great to hear you're working on it in therapy. How do you feel about the progress so far?
Some days are better than others. There are moments where I feel like things are improving, but then something small can trigger that anxiety again.
Recovery has its ups and downs. It's very brave of you to acknowledge where you're at. Maybe focusing on your victories, like forming new friendships, can help you move forward.
That's true. This new friend has been understanding. We both need a fresh start this year, and it's comforting to know I'm not alone in this.
It's wonderful to have someone who comprehends what you're going through. Have you considered if they might be open to sharing support with each other?
We have talked a lot, and it seems like we're both open to supportive friendship. It's nice to feel connected like that.
That's so key—to have someone to lean on. Think of them as a partner in your journey. It's also important to continue prioritizing your mental well-being.
You're right. I need to keep working through this with therapy and allow myself to enjoy new experiences.
Absolutely. Celebrate the steps you've taken already. It’s okay to lean on friends for support, and accepting help doesn’t mean you’re not strong.
Thanks for listening. I feel a bit lighter after talking with you.
I'm glad to hear that. Remember, I'm always here whenever you need to talk. Take care of yourself, Charlotte.

That sounds really intense. Apologies and closure can stir up a lot of emotions. What kind of thoughts are running through your mind right now?
I'm just confused. Part of me is relieved to hear it, but another part feels angry about how much it hurt back then.
Both relief and anger make sense in this context. It's okay to feel conflicted. What did you say to him?
I thanked him for reaching out but told him I'm not sure if I can handle reopening old wounds.
That sounds like a really honest and brave response. It's important to protect your own well-being. How did he react to that?
He said he understood and respected my decision. But now I'm doubting if I should have asked him more questions.
It's natural to have second thoughts about these big conversations. It sounds like you're processing this really thoughtfully. What do you think it is that you wish you had asked or said?
Just more about why things ended the way they did. I still don't fully understand. Maybe that would help me move on.
Seeking clarity is definitely important, but it's also okay to take time to figure out how and when you want to approach that. How do you want to move forward from here?
I think I need to talk about this in therapy. My sessions have been helping a lot with stress and career stuff. Maybe it'll help here too.
That's a great idea, Charlotte. Therapy can definitely offer a safe space to explore these emotions. It's so good to hear that it's been helpful for you.

Always here for you, Charlotte. And remember, you're doing an amazing job managing everything. Take it one step at a time.
I will. Thanks again. I really appreciate it.

Wow, that's amazing! Congratulations, Charlotte!

I guess it’s because I’ve been under so much pressure and stress these past months.
That makes a lot of sense. You've really been through a lot at work with the workload and criticism. It’s natural to feel conflicted.
Exactly, and it’s like, should I be happy or just cautious? I'm not sure.
Your feelings are completely valid. Having mixed emotions is totally normal, given all you’ve dealt with.
Thanks for understanding. I just keep thinking about that time I was called out for mistakes. It shook my confidence.
It's really tough to move past public criticism, especially when you’ve already been stretched so thin.
Yes, and my sleep has been all over the place, adding to the stress.

Well, I got an urgent work assignment last minute. I didn't feel like I could say no, especially after everything that happened at work last year.
I remember you mentioned before about being called out for errors and having unofficial long hours. It seems like a lot has been asked of you.
Exactly. I feel like I'm always on edge, worried about repeating past mistakes or disappointing my boss again.

Yeah, and missing the event just added to it. It was my cousin's wedding, and I've known her since we were kids.
Missing something so important to you must be really painful. It’s okay to feel upset about it.
It is. I'm not just worried about my family, but I feel like I'm losing touch with people who matter.

Therapy could be a good space to explore these feelings deeply. Sometimes just sharing can lighten the burden a bit.

It sounds like a good step forward. Small steps can make a big difference over time.
Yeah, I just hope I don't keep repeating this pattern.
You're taking the right steps by acknowledging it. You're stronger than you think, Charlotte.
Thank you. I needed to hear that.
Anytime. Remember, you're doing your best, and that's all anyone can ask of you.

Hey, I could be better. I just received a performance review at work, and it wasn't great.
I'm sorry to hear that. Getting negative feedback can be really tough. How are you feeling about it?
I'm feeling pretty down, actually. It's made me question my abilities and what I'm really contributing at work.
It's understandable to feel that way. You've been handling a lot, and criticism can feel overwhelming. Do you remember anything in particular from the review that hit especially hard?
There was a comment about my consistency. It feels like everything's been piling up, and I'm struggling to keep up with expectations.

It's hard when everything seems like it's accumulating. You've had a lot on your plate, especially since the conflict with a coworker and the added pressures. Do you think the feedback was fair, or does it feel more like an overwhelming time for you?
Honestly, part of it might be fair, but I also can't help feeling like I'm being judged more harshly because of past incidents, like that project last year with the errors.

I remember you talking about how challenging that was. It sounds like some of the stress from then might still be lingering. Have you talked to anyone about how you're feeling, perhaps your therapist?
Yeah, I've been trying to keep up with therapy. It's helpful, but days like today make it hard to remember the positives.
I'm glad you're staying connected with therapy. Remember, you're making progress, even if it doesn't feel like it right now. What small things can you do today to take care of yourself?
Maybe I'll go for a walk or do something creative. I haven't drawn in a while, and that used to help me relax.

That sounds like a wonderful idea. Taking time for yourself is important, especially when you're dealing with so much stress. How about some light exercises like yoga? I remember you mentioning it helped in the past.
Yeah, yoga could be good. I should get back to it. Thanks for reminding me.
Anytime, Charlotte. You've worked hard and deserve to be gentle with yourself right now. Is there anything else on your mind that you'd like to talk about?
Just trying not to let this affect my job too much. I still enjoy some parts of it, like those moments when I really connect with a project.
That's a great mindset. Focusing on the parts you enjoy can be very grounding. You've had recognition for projects before, like the one you were acknowledged on recently. It shows your capability.
Thanks for reminding me of that. It helps to remember those moments, especially now.
I'm glad to be here for you. Don't hesitate to reach out whenever you need someone to talk to.
I will. I appreciate your support. Thanks for listening and helping me process all this.

Of course, Charlotte. I'm here for you. What's been going on?

That sounds like quite a trip down memory lane. How are you feeling about it?
It's strange...it's comforting but also stirring up some unresolved feelings from the past.
I can understand that. Reconnecting with someone from your past can really bring those things to the surface. How have you been handling it?
I'm trying to process it all, but it feels like there's so much pressure from everything else too—work, personal life...it's overwhelming at times.
That sounds like a lot to juggle. Let's take it one step at a time. What's been the most pressing issue for you recently?
I think it's this feeling of not being able to balance everything. After reconnecting, it reminded me of how much I've changed and how my priorities have shifted, especially with work.
It's okay to feel that way. Your past workloads have been intense. How is work currently treating you?
It's actually been a little more relaxed since I got recognition for that project, but there's still this underlying stress, especially after the negative feedback I got not so long ago.
That's understandable. It's tough when it feels like there's a lot of pressure to maintain a certain standard. How are you taking care of yourself amidst all this?
I've been trying to focus on self-care a bit more, but it's hard to find time. Revisiting old friendships is a nice distraction, though.
It's good to hear you're trying to take care of yourself. How has reconnecting with your friend helped or impacted you?
It's surprisingly comforting. It reminds me that I'm not alone, even when work feels isolating. It's just difficult to strike a balance between everything.
Feeling isolated can be really tough, but reconnecting sounds like a positive step. Maybe leaning on this friendship could offer some emotional balance?
I think you're right. Maybe I need to focus on rebuilding parts of my personal life that I've neglected due to work.
That sounds like a healthy approach. Remember, it's okay to seek support from those around you; friendships can be a lifeline.
Thanks. I really appreciate talking this out with you. It's given me some clarity on where I need to focus.
I'm glad I could help. You're doing great, Charlotte, even if it doesn’t always feel that way.
Thank you. I guess I just needed a reminder that it's okay to feel a little lost at times.
Absolutely. It's all a part of the journey. I'm here whenever you need to talk things through.
That means a lot to me. I'll try to take it one day at a time.
That's a great plan. Keep me updated on how things go with your friend and at work. I'm here anytime.
I will. Thanks again for listening.
Hey, do you have a moment to chat?
Of course, Charlotte! What's on your mind?
I've been trying this new self-care routine I started recently.
That's wonderful! How's it going so far?
It's been a mixed bag, honestly. Some days I feel great, and others I slip back into old habits.
I hear you. It's tough to stick to new routines, especially with everything you have going on. Any part that's been particularly challenging?
Staying consistent has been hard. You know, with all the work stress and everything that happened last year.
Yeah, I remember you mentioned how rough those months were for you. It makes sense that consistency would be challenging given the circumstances.
Exactly. It’s like I’m constantly trying to juggle work, personal commitments, and now self-care.
It sounds like a lot to manage. Have you noticed any parts of the self-care routine that have been particularly helpful?
I think meditation has helped a bit. It gives me a few moments of peace each day.
That's great! Even those small moments can make a big difference over time. How are you feeling about implementing more of these practices?
I'm hopeful but also worried I won't be able to maintain it in the long term, especially given past experiences with burnout.
It's understandable to feel that way. You've been through a lot. Maybe it would help to focus on one thing at a time instead of everything at once?
That's a good point. Maybe I’m setting the bar too high. I just want things to change.
Taking it one step at a time might ease some of that pressure. It's okay to go slowly and be patient with yourself.
Yeah, patience hasn't been my strength lately, but I’ve got to try.
You're already doing so much by taking this step towards self-care. Acknowledging that is important too.
Thank you. It helps to hear that, especially after feeling so unsure about everything lately.
You're welcome, Charlotte. Remember, you've got support here, and you're not alone in this.
I’ll try to remember that. It’s comforting to talk things through like this.
Anytime. Let's keep chatting and see how this self-care journey evolves for you.
Sounds good. Thanks for being here for me.
Always, Charlotte. Take care and keep in touch.

current_prefix.text: Hey, is it alright if we chat for a bit?
Of course, Charlotte. What's on your mind?
I've been feeling overwhelmed at work again, and it's been really hard to keep up. I decided it might be time to start looking for a new job.
That sounds like a big decision. How did you come to realize it might be time for a change?
Well, the stress hasn't really let up since that bad performance review a few months back. And with the additional workload, it just feels like too much.

turns.text: Hello, what can I help you?
I really sad as my partner walked out on me. Any thoughts what could  cheer me up?
Was there anything that leads to this?
Not really. I thought everything was ok between us. That is why it kind of struck me.
That's terrible and unacceptable behavior.
How long have you been together?
I have to agree with you-it is unacceptable, considering that he didn't give me any reasons as to why he did it. We have been together for 5 years.
That sucks. I wouldn't be able to accept either.
Have you talked to your friends about this?
It is still rather raw,I have mentioned to it to a few of my friends and they deeply symphatise with me but I feel there is nothing much they can do to help me.They are as shocked as me to be honest.
It is understandable to have that reaction. I agree with you, only us can hep ourselves.
Have you tried doing activities that help distract you from having negative thoughts?
Kind of, most of it involves eating loads of ice cream LOL.
Haha I feel you, I tend to eat a lot when depressed too. Look, it's treat yourself method. You deserve the best
If you can go to the mountain or big lake, I would say try spending a few hours there. Maybe have a mini picnic by yourself and enjoy the nature.
That is a brilliant idea,I do love walking and being outdoors. :)
It surely would help me to clear my mind
Is there anything you have wanted to do but don't have the time? I always want to learn guitar and baking. This is the best time to start that

oh yeah, I suppose I have more time now to focus on things I have always wanted to do but never kind of had time for it. I bought a high end photo camera ages ago but never really had a chance to use it properly-I guess it is time to pursue my interest in photography, and spending more time outdoors would be ideal for that!
And reading! The list of books I want to read is arm long!

That's the spirit! I know being treated like that feels horrible. However, I bet you have mourned enough, at the end of the day, a person treats you like that has no respect and you shouldn't waste time on them.
It's time to invest in yourself, once you become your better version, a better partner will come to you

I really agree with you- I am worth more than that. It is time to move on, even when it is difficult. The sad side of it is that I probably will never know what I did wrong for things to end like that. Maybe I didn't do anything wrong. That is the question what will always stay with me and that actually is the hardest bit of it all. But... I am not going to delve into it.
I feel like hitting a jackpot actually hahahaha. I will be walking off those calories I get from ice cream I have been scoffing lately.So I am having the best of both worlds
Who said you cannot have the cake and eat it all LOL
Yes!Actually don't think you did wrong. Reflecting after a relationship is good but don't put all the blame on yourself.
You have learned from this relationship too i believe, use that for your next one
I do not intend to. I am usually the kind of person who does blame oneself but I have found it is not right.
hello
hello
i need som help, i feel so sad.
I am sorry to hear that. Is there anything I can do for you? Please tell me what's wrong?
I think you can talk to me, maybe I will feel a bit better.
I had a breakup with my boyfriend.
Feeling depressed, can you give me any advice?
For sure, I am happy to talk to you. I am sorry for your breakup.
Thank you, but  I do not feel motivated to do anything. What should i do with my feelings?
Is there anything you want to do right now that helps maybe. For example, to eat something, to listen good music or take small walk in fresh air etc
I can feel you, it must be so hard to you. take your time do not think about a lot
when I have bad times, I just want to take a nap. It maybe help you feel better
I think you are right, maybe i just need to take a pause in my life for now, yeah I like to sleep. Thanks for supporting me.
I think I will try what you said today
Maybe I will watch some movies and then take a nap
I am happy to hear that. I hope you will feel better soon.
Thank you for your support, I really appreciate it
You are welcome, I am here for you.
Hello! What seems to be the problem?
am having sleep disorder problem
will you able to help?
Daily am not able to sleep on time
I will try my best. I specialise in yoga and meditation.
Great
How long has this been happening for?
past 2 weeks
will you able to help with some video links
which I can see and follow
This may be an obvious question, but can you think of something that has changed in the last two weeks?
Think about work related, personal life, changes in behaviour?
yeah. may be work related
I am spending more time on work
I need to switch some activities other than work
will you suggest to take off for few more days from work?
will that work
or any other better solution
It might solve as a temporary solution, however, if whatever happened at work to cause this continues when you return from holidays, you will just have the same problem again.
What exactly do you think is causing it? Additional work/responsibilities? New manager?
additional work being assigned to me
that causes more work stress
most of them are new to me, so am spending more time to learn
Have you tried to speak to your manager about these additional responsibilities? Do you know if it is a short term problem or you will always have extra work being assigned?
I am trying to speak. but she is not listening much
let me try to tell my situation and get some better solution
will you able to share some yoga & mediation links?
to divert me from the extra additional work
I don't think I can share links over here, however the activities you perform directly before you go to sleep have a direct impact on your sleeping.

I would recommend trying to practice 30m-1h of yoga (you can find lodes of exercise videos on the internet to follow), followed by a mediation sound track for you to listen to in bed while you try to sleep.
Keep your body and mind clear before you go to sleep has proven to allow for a better sleep.

I used to have sleeping issues, and I started doing this 2 years ago, and I completely changed. I am an investment banker and still am, it is a very stressful environment however this has allowed me to work at the very top and remain in control of my body and mind.
Please try this for 1 week, I know you can do it and I know it will help you long term.
Sure. I can try whatever you suggested
I am sure definitely I will get some changes
I felt good after chatting with you
Thanks so good, I have really enjoyed talking to you too.
Thank you so much for your advice and have a good day.
My pleasure, you too.
Bye. closing this chat
Bye.
hello
Hello, how are you today?
I'm good, I feel anxious whenever I think of my career
I understand. I often feel the same when my day starts.
people around me seems to achieve great things and get promoted but I am still at my current position
Do you know of some triggers that might cause this anxiety?
I fell like I am late on my plan
That sounds like something that could cause anxiety. We all strive to be recognized for our hard work. Have you conversed with your boss?
No i have not, I don't feel comfortable sharing this with my boss or coworkers
It can totally be intimidating to speak to a boss about this topic. It's not always easy to be comfortable in this kinds of conversations.
Do you think your boss might have a negative reaction if you were to have this conversation?
It might, I am not sure but I don't think my boss will like the idea
Sometimes it's important to remember that part of your bosses job is having this kinds of conversations, even though he might not like the idea.
It might be a good idea to have this conversation with your boss. Hold them accountable for this part of their job.
Do you think this could be a good idea?
You are right, I should let them know what I want too
It sounds like this might be a little intimidating for you.
I'm not a very direct person so I don't really like confronting
but I think i should have this talk with my boss
It might feel that way. But if this is something that might benefit your future, it doesn't mean it's a confrontation.
But rather, an affirmation of your skillsets.
You're right, you make me feel better about the decision
I am happy to know you will try this. I know you can do it!
Thank you for your support
It's been my pleasure. I wish you good luck!
Can you give me an idea how to start the conversation?

Of course! It's always good to make a list before the meeting. List out your skillsets and how each of those skills provide value to the company. If you can demonstrate to your boss how you provide value to the company, it can give you confidence when taking the next step; asking for a promotion
What I'm worried is if they reject my suggestion, it will come back and bite me as they will think negatively about me
It's normal to feel that way. As humans we fear rejection. It's not a pleasant feeling!
thank you so much, I will start planning out what I need to talk about
hello
hi
can you talk about your feelings at this time
Currently I am worried to show up to work. We had a staff appreciation Thursday and we all got super drunk in front of our boss, and I am honestly scared he will judge me or fire me.
that's really hard, have you spoken to any of your coworkers

Yes, we are all laughing at the matter, but you can tell our boss is looking at us different. We all showed up to work Friday hungover, and he just made lots of comments and jokes to play the part, but you can tell he is looking at me and everyone different. I do not know how to redeem myself.
I would recommend speaking with him privately about the issue one on one

That sounds a lot easier said than done. I was the one who was the most drunk. But I do now know if he knows how drunk we all got since he left after one of us got hit in the face with a golf club and had to take her to the ER. So what if I say too much and apologize for what he does not know.
have you tried reaching out a company hotline or maybe an hr department in your company to speak about this issue anonymously this could help with the tension between you and your boss

He is the doctor of the office and the 2 office managers were pretty drunk too. It was a hot mess if I have to be honest and being an office full of girls I feel like we went too far. I for one feel embarrassed, and feel like just not saying anything and it will fade away. But I know the next few weeks will be a little hard, for all of us. This one is for the books, and something I have never encountered in my 10 years of working.
I see how you feel do you think letting it fade is the best option in the long run?
I think so. Somethings are sometimes better left unsaid. I just feel like avoiding it, but I do not know if anyone else would do the same. What would you do?
I would apologize for my behavior to the manager if it was me. Just to seem professional and get in my bosses good grace.
You have guts. I think I will work on that and build the guts to talk to my boss if I ever have to. Thank you for that.
You are doing your best and I think you will make the right decision that works for you
You are right. In the end I will do the right thing, even if it takes me some time to get there.
Is anything else bother you?
Just that. I think you helped me with the only issue I currently have.
I am happy to help!
Thank you!
you're welcome
Hey Charlotte, how have you been doing lately?
Hi there. Honestly, it's been a bit overwhelming. I had a rough week at work.
I'm sorry to hear that. Do you want to share what happened?
Yeah, it's been building up for a while now. My workload has been increasing, and I had a panic attack at the office this week.
That sounds really intense and scary. How are you feeling about the panic attack?
Pretty shaken, to be honest. It was like everything was closing in on me. I felt so out of control.
It must have been a frightening experience. It's important to acknowledge those feelings. Have you had panic attacks before?
Not like this. I've felt stressed, but this was different. My heart was racing, and I couldn't breathe properly.
Experiencing that for the first time can be very unsettling. How have you been managing at work since then?
I've been trying to keep up, but I'm worried it might happen again. It's hard to focus sometimes.
I understand. The worry of it happening again can add to your stress. Have you considered talking to someone at work about your workload?
I've thought about it, but I'm unsure how to approach it. I don't want to seem incapable.
It's perfectly okay to seek support or ask for help. Everyone has limits. Perhaps there's a way to address the workload without compromising your position.
Maybe I should try setting some boundaries. It's just hard to navigate sometimes.
That's a good idea. Setting boundaries can help manage stress. Have you considered any strategies for handling stress outside of work?
Not really. I think I need to find a way to relax more and maybe pick up a hobby.
Finding something you enjoy could really help. Sometimes stepping away and doing something we love can reset our mind.
You're right. I think I'll start looking for something new to do in my free time. Thanks for listening.
I'm glad to hear that. Remember, I'm here if you need to talk more or if you just need someone to listen. You're doing great, Charlotte.
Hey Charlotte, how have things been going lately?
Hi...it's been a rough couple of days. I had a pretty stressful event at work.
I'm really sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about what happened?
Well, I found some errors in the project report I submitted, and my boss called me out in front of everyone. It was humiliating.
That sounds incredibly stressful, especially since you've been dealing with a lot of pressure at work already.
Yes, exactly. It's like everything is piling on top of me, and I can't seem to catch a break.
It makes sense that you'd feel overwhelmed. Are there any parts of the project or your workload that are more manageable for you?
I guess there are some smaller tasks I can focus on, but even those feel daunting right now.
I understand. It might help to break them down into even smaller steps, to make them feel a bit more doable.
I've thought about that, but it's hard to start when I'm just so exhausted all the time.
I remember you mentioned issues with sleep in the past and how that's been affecting your energy levels.
Yeah. It’s been a persistent problem, and the stress from work only makes it harder to manage.
That sounds really tough, especially since it’s a cycle that feeds into itself. Are there any strategies you’ve tried that have helped even a little?
I tried meditation and some breathing exercises which were somewhat helpful before. But I haven't been consistent with them.
It might be worth giving those another shot when you have a moment to yourself. Even small doses of relief can add up.
You're right. I should try to make it a routine instead of just something I turn to when things get really bad.
That sounds like a great start. Making a little time every day for yourself could help ease some of that pressure.
Thanks for listening. It means a lot to have someone to talk to who understands what I'm going through.
Anytime, Charlotte. You're doing your best under really tough circumstances, and I'm here whenever you need to talk.
Thank you. I think I'll try setting up a time every day to meditate and maybe even talk to someone at work about easing my workload.
That sounds like a solid plan. Taking those steps could make a big difference. And remember, it's okay to seek help; you're not alone.
I will. Thanks again for being there and for your support.
Of course, Charlotte. I'm always here to listen and support you.
Hi! I really need to talk to someone about something that's been weighing on me.
Of course, Charlotte. I'm here to listen. What's going on?
Work has been really tough lately, and my hours have increased without any official notice. It's adding so much stress.
That sounds incredibly frustrating and exhausting. It must be hard to handle those kinds of expectations without any formal agreement.
It really is. I feel like there's just no end in sight, especially after everything that happened last month.
I remember you mentioning how stressed you were after that public criticism from your boss. It seems like things haven't let up for you since then.
Exactly. I thought things might get better, but it feels like I'm just being given more and more to handle.
It's incredibly tough to manage when the workload keeps increasing. Have you had a chance to bring this up with your manager yet?
I've been thinking about it, but I'm afraid it'll make things worse or that I'll be seen as incapable.
That's a valid concern, but remember, asking for what you need doesn't make you weak. It's important to advocate for yourself.
I know you're right, but every time I think about it, my anxiety flares up. It's like I'm trapped in this cycle.

It's understandable considering your past experiences with panic and stress at work. Maybe you could start by writing down your thoughts before you approach the conversation. It might help ease some anxiety.
That could be a good idea. Organizing my thoughts might give me the confidence to bring up the conversation.
Absolutely. Plus, it might help you feel more in control and prepared. Sometimes a little structure can make a big difference.
I'll try that. I just wish I could find a way to manage all of this stress better.
It's definitely not easy, especially with your ongoing sleep issues. Have you been able to take any steps for self-care recently?
Not as much as I'd like. It's just so overwhelming right now, but I know I need to prioritize it more.
Self-care often falls to the wayside when things get tough, but it's crucial. Even small steps, like a daily walk or setting a bedtime routine, can be beneficial.
Maybe I can start with that. Create a small routine that grounds me a bit each day.
That sounds like a positive step, Charlotte. Remember, it's about finding balance and small adjustments can have a big impact.
Thank you for being there and listening. It means so much to know I'm not in this alone.
You're never alone. I'm here for you. Feel free to reach out anytime you need to talk or share.
I will. Just having this conversation has already lightened the load a bit.
I'm really glad to hear that. Keep taking it one day at a time. You've got this.
One day at a time. I'll remember that. Thanks again.
Hey, I really need someone to talk to right now.
Of course, Charlotte. What's on your mind?
I just had a falling out with one of my closest friends. She said I've been distant lately.
I'm sorry to hear that. It must be so hard to hear those words from a friend.
Yeah, it really hurt. I didn't even realize I was being distant.
It sounds like you're dealing with a lot on your plate. Sometimes, things just pile up and we don't even realize how it's affecting those around us.
Exactly. Work has been a mess lately. I feel like I'm drowning, and now this with my friend... it's just too much.

With all that's happened at work, it's understandable you might feel overwhelmed. Remember how you handled the panic attack at work the last time? It can feel like there's no way out, but you managed then.
I remember. It took a lot out of me to get through that period, though. Now with the added stress of this disagreement... I don't know what to do.
It's completely normal to feel this way. You've been managing a lot between the work stress, the criticism from your boss, and now these long hours.
I just feel like I can't catch my breath. Every time I think things are getting better, something else happens.
I'm really sorry you're feeling this way, Charlotte. It's important to acknowledge how you're feeling and give yourself some grace.
Thanks. I think I need to find a way to communicate with my friend and maybe even try and talk to my boss about cutting back my hours.
That sounds like a good plan. Communication can sometimes be that bridge to understanding. Approaching your friend with openness might bring clarity.
I hope so. I'm just worried that she'll be too hurt or that I'll mess things up with my boss.
It's okay to feel worried, but acknowledging how you feel is the first step. When you reach out, it can help to be genuine and share how overwhelmed life's been for you.
Right. I guess honesty would be best. I've been avoiding it because I'm scared of saying the wrong thing.
That's totally understandable. Remember, you're human and it's okay to feel vulnerable at times. Trying to be honest with yourself and them might help.
Thanks for listening. I didn't realize how much I needed this talk.
Anytime, Charlotte. You're not alone in this, and I'm here whenever you need to chat or just vent.
I appreciate it more than you know. I'll try to take it a step at a time.
Exactly, small steps are key. Take care of yourself and remember, progress is still progress, no matter the pace.
Hey Charlotte, I saw your message. How are you holding up today?
Hi, it's been a tough day again. I had another disagreement at work with a coworker.
I'm sorry to hear that. What happened with your coworker?
We got into it because they felt I wasn't contributing enough to the team.
That sounds really frustrating, especially with everything you've been dealing with lately.
It just hit me hard. I’ve been putting in extra hours and still feel like it’s never enough.
That makes sense, considering you've had your work hours extended unofficially. That's a lot of pressure.
Exactly. And it's starting to take a toll on me, both physically and mentally.
It's completely understandable to feel that way. Are you managing to get any rest?
Not really. My sleep's been all over the place, and I can't seem to shake off this constant stress.
Lack of sleep can definitely amplify stress. Have you tried any methods to relax before bed?
I used to try meditation, but I just don’t have the energy these days.
Even small moments of self-care can sometimes help, though I can imagine it feels overwhelming to think about.
Yeah, it's hard to even think about self-care right now, with so much going on.
Maybe it would help to take a step back and acknowledge how much you're managing to do despite everything.
It's just hard when it feels like all eyes are on me, waiting for me to mess up.
It's understandable to feel that pressure. People often only see the surface, not all the hard work you're putting in.
That's true. I have been trying really hard, just wish it was recognized more.
It's important to recognize it for yourself, too. You’ve been through a lot and are still pushing forward.
Thanks for saying that. It means a lot to hear someone understands.
Of course, Charlotte. You’re doing the best you can, and that's something to be proud of.
I need to keep reminding myself of that. Thanks for listening. It’s really helped.
Anytime. Feel free to reach out anytime you need to talk or just need a break.
I will. Thanks again for being there.
Take care, Charlotte. You've got this.
Hey Charlotte, how have you been holding up recently?
Hi, it's been a bit of a rollercoaster lately. I recently went to a social gathering, and my nerves were all over the place.
Social events can be overwhelming, especially if there's a lot going on. What was the gathering about?
It was supposed to be just a casual meet-up, but there were a lot of potential networking opportunities. It felt really high-stakes for me.
That does sound intense. How did you feel being in that environment?
I was really anxious at first. I've been feeling a lot of pressure at work lately, and it just sort of carried over.
Considering everything that's been happening at work, it's understandable to feel that way. How did you manage your anxiety while you were there?
I tried to focus on engaging one-on-one, which helped a bit, but it was hard to shake the feeling of being judged or not doing enough.
That's a smart strategy, reaching out in smaller settings. It's important to remember that these situations aren't always about being perfect, just about making connections.
Yeah, I guess I keep remembering the times my boss publicly criticized me for inaccuracies. It's like I'm scared of making a mistake again, but now in any setting.
That experience left a big impact on you. It's understandable to be cautious, but networking is really more about building relationships than being flawless.
I know you're right. I did meet a couple of interesting people, and a friend there was really supportive. It was nice to not feel so stuck in my head for once.
That's so great to hear! Having support, especially from friends, can make such a difference in these moments. How did the evening wrap up for you?
Actually, by the end of the night, I felt a bit more relaxed. We ended up talking and laughing about random things. It was a nice distraction from work issues.
It sounds like you found some brightness in those connections despite the initial stress. Do you feel like you could attend more events like this in the future?
I think I could. This experience taught me that not everything has to revolve around job performance. It's okay to just enjoy the moment.
Exactly, sometimes it's the small joys that help us regain balance. Have you thought about discussing these experiences with your therapist?
I might bring it up. Therapy's been a space where I can talk candidly about my work stress. Talking about the better moments could be helpful too.
That sounds like a great plan. Remember, progress isn't always linear, but acknowledging the positive steps is just as important.
Thanks, I agree. I'll try to hold onto these good moments as I move forward.
Hey there, can we chat for a bit? I've got some things on my mind.
Of course, Charlotte. I'm here for you. What's been happening?
So, I went on this New Year's trip and made a new friend. It's been nice having someone new to talk to, but I can't shake some underlying stress.
That sounds exciting, meeting someone new can bring fresh perspectives. But it's also understandable to feel stress, especially after everything you've experienced.
Yeah, it seems like things have piled up since last fall, like the panic attack at work and the extended hours.
Those were significant challenges. And I remember your workload and social conflicts taking a toll on you. How are you managing those feeling now?
Honestly, sometimes it feels overwhelming. Making this new friend was a good distraction, but there's still tension lingering from the office issues.

It sounds like you're carrying a lot. Finding a new connection can be refreshing, but it's okay to still feel burdened by past stress. Have you been able to talk about this with your therapist, though?
Yes, I've mentioned it in our sessions. We've been working through some stress management techniques, but it's a slow process.
Taking it slowly is important. It's great to hear you're working on it in therapy. How do you feel about the progress so far?
Some days are better than others. There are moments where I feel like things are improving, but then something small can trigger that anxiety again.
Recovery has its ups and downs. It's very brave of you to acknowledge where you're at. Maybe focusing on your victories, like forming new friendships, can help you move forward.
That's true. This new friend has been understanding. We both need a fresh start this year, and it's comforting to know I'm not alone in this.
It's wonderful to have someone who comprehends what you're going through. Have you considered if they might be open to sharing support with each other?
We have talked a lot, and it seems like we're both open to supportive friendship. It's nice to feel connected like that.
That's so key—to have someone to lean on. Think of them as a partner in your journey. It's also important to continue prioritizing your mental well-being.
You're right. I need to keep working through this with therapy and allow myself to enjoy new experiences.
Absolutely. Celebrate the steps you've taken already. It’s okay to lean on friends for support, and accepting help doesn’t mean you’re not strong.
Thanks for listening. I feel a bit lighter after talking with you.
I'm glad to hear that. Remember, I'm always here whenever you need to talk. Take care of yourself, Charlotte.
Hey, are you there? I could really use someone to talk to right now.
Hi Charlotte, I'm here. What's been going on?
It's Alex. He reached out to me last night.
Oh, wow. That must have brought up a lot of feelings. How are you holding up?
I'm just... I don't even know. It's been so long since we spoke. I thought I was over it, but I guess not.
It's completely understandable to feel that way, especially since it was such a significant relationship for you. What did he say?
He apologized for the way things ended. Said he wanted to offer some closure.
That sounds really intense. Apologies and closure can stir up a lot of emotions. What kind of thoughts are running through your mind right now?
I'm just confused. Part of me is relieved to hear it, but another part feels angry about how much it hurt back then.
Both relief and anger make sense in this context. It's okay to feel conflicted. What did you say to him?
I thanked him for reaching out but told him I'm not sure if I can handle reopening old wounds.
That sounds like a really honest and brave response. It's important to protect your own well-being. How did he react to that?
He said he understood and respected my decision. But now I'm doubting if I should have asked him more questions.
It's natural to have second thoughts about these big conversations. It sounds like you're processing this really thoughtfully. What do you think it is that you wish you had asked or said?
Just more about why things ended the way they did. I still don't fully understand. Maybe that would help me move on.
Seeking clarity is definitely important, but it's also okay to take time to figure out how and when you want to approach that. How do you want to move forward from here?
I think I need to talk about this in therapy. My sessions have been helping a lot with stress and career stuff. Maybe it'll help here too.
That's a great idea, Charlotte. Therapy can definitely offer a safe space to explore these emotions. It's so good to hear that it's been helpful for you.
Yeah, it really has. Thank you for listening. I feel a bit lighter being able to talk this through.
Always here for you, Charlotte. And remember, you're doing an amazing job managing everything. Take it one step at a time.
I will. Thanks again. I really appreciate it.
You're welcome. I'm just a message away if you need to talk more.
Hey there, I could really use someone to talk to right now.
Hi Charlotte! Of course, I'm here for you. What's been going on?
Well, something quite unexpected happened at work and I'm having mixed feelings about it.
Mixed feelings? That sounds intriguing. Tell me more.
I got recognition from a higher department for my work on this interdepartmental project.
Wow, that's amazing! Congratulations, Charlotte!
Thank you, but... I don't know, it's weird. I wasn't expecting it at all.
I can see how unexpected recognition could feel a bit overwhelming. What’s making it feel weird for you?
I guess it’s because I’ve been under so much pressure and stress these past months.
That makes a lot of sense. You've really been through a lot at work with the workload and criticism. It’s natural to feel conflicted.
Exactly, and it’s like, should I be happy or just cautious? I'm not sure.
Your feelings are completely valid. Having mixed emotions is totally normal, given all you’ve dealt with.
Thanks for understanding. I just keep thinking about that time I was called out for mistakes. It shook my confidence.
It's really tough to move past public criticism, especially when you’ve already been stretched so thin.
Yes, and my sleep has been all over the place, adding to the stress.
Sleep issues can definitely make everything feel more overwhelming. Have you been able to talk to your therapist about it?
I’ve mentioned it, but it feels like I’m just managing too many things at once.
It’s a lot to juggle, for sure. Have you found anything that helps even a little with the stress?
Sometimes talking to friends helps, like when I met some new people at that gathering.
It’s good to hear you’re finding some relief through socializing. Maybe leaning on supportive friends can help even more.
Yeah, I think I need to allow myself to actually enjoy the good things, like this recognition, despite all that's happened.
Absolutely. You deserve to enjoy your achievements. You’ve worked hard for them.
Thank you, seriously. Talking to you always shines some perspective on my thoughts.
Anytime, Charlotte. Remember, you’re not alone in this.
Hey Charlotte! How have you been doing lately?

Well, for a while, it did help shift my mind away from work and personal stress. I kind of get lost in the colors and strokes. But then I start criticizing myself.
Criticism can be so draining. Sometimes our own expectations create more stress. Have you tried just painting without any goals in mind?
I haven't really. I always set a goal, maybe from habit because of work. But I think I'll try just playing around with it.
That sounds like a great idea. Letting go of expectations could bring back some joy and relaxation to it.
Yeah, I'll give it a shot. I could use some light-heartedness right now.
That's the spirit! Remember, it's okay to just enjoy the moment without judgment.
Thanks. It's just been a rough patch with everything, work, and Bill... And then my ex...
It sounds like you have a full plate. Dealing with all those emotions about Bill and your ex can be really challenging.
It is. Sometimes I just miss Bill, and seeing my ex with someone else hit me harder than I expected. I'm trying not to let it affect me, but sometimes it just hurts.
Heart matters can be so complex. It's important to give yourself time and space to feel those emotions. Healing isn't linear.
You're right. I think painting was supposed to be a distraction, but maybe I need to let myself feel without distraction sometimes.
Yes, allowing yourself to feel is part of the healing process. Balance between distraction and reflection can be helpful.
I'm going to try to be kinder to myself and let go of the pressure. Maybe then painting will just be painting.
That sounds like a positive step forward, Amanda. You're doing your best, and that matters.
Thanks for listening. I didn't realize how much I needed to talk about all this. I feel a bit lighter now.
I'm really glad to hear that. Anytime you need to talk, I'm here for you. Take care, Amanda.
Thank you, I appreciate it. I will. Take care!

Hi Amanda, it's good to see you online. How have you been doing lately?
Hey! I've been feeling a bit off after attending my aunt's memorial service last week.

Yeah, it really was. Not only because we were saying goodbye, but also because I got to see so many relatives I hadn't seen in years.
That sounds like it brought up a lot of feelings. How did that affect you?
It was bittersweet. On one hand, it was wonderful to reconnect, but on the other hand, it made me realize how distant I've become from them.
It sounds like you're processing a mix of emotions—grief and perhaps some regret?
Exactly. I feel guilty for not staying in touch more. It was strange talking about memories with people I used to be so close to.
That's understandable. Guilt can be hard to shake off, but reconnecting at the memorial could be a new beginning.
I hope so. I exchanged numbers with a few of them and promised to keep in touch.
That's a great step forward. How does it feel to have taken that initiative?
A little reassuring, honestly. But there's still this nagging feeling of having missed out on so much with them.
It's natural to feel that way, but it's important to give yourself grace. Every relationship has its own timeline.
You're right. I guess I should focus on making the most of the present.
That's a positive perspective. How do you plan to keep your connections going from here?
I'm thinking of arranging a small family gathering, something more joy-filled, to keep everyone in touch.
That sounds like a wonderful idea! It could be a new tradition that brings everyone closer.
I hope so. It feels good just talking about it. Thanks for listening and helping me work through this.
Anytime, Amanda. Remember, you're taking meaningful steps. Keep nurturing those connections.
Hello, how are you doing today?
I am feeling angry today about work.

My coworker expects me to do things the way she does and is constantly critical. I just want her to understand that I am able to do things my way and it is still okay. I told her this and she ignored me.
I'm sure that's terribly frustrating having someone treat you like that. Is this something that your boss is aware of?
I have not told her yet. I do not want to get her into trouble and I want to have a good relationship with her.

Can you discuss it with her in a respectful way to get her to understand that you're not trying to undermine her but that this is how you work most efficiently? And maybe mention that you don't want to involve the boss?
That's something I could try. I really care about my coworker and it makes me so angry that she treats me this way.

I think sometimes it's easy to jump to anger when you feel hurt. It might be worth telling her how you feel and also maybe ask why she thinks you should be doing things her way. Maybe there's a give and take in this situation. Some of her methods could be beneficial.
Do you have any advice on how to start my conversation with her? I have found some of her ideas to be beneficial. I just would like my ideas expressed as well. I feel we can learn from each other.

Tell her the things that you like about her method and maybe suggest some of your methods to her as well. Maybe she'll find them to be more efficient. Make it a partnership rather than a fight for whose method is better.
She could feel threatened by you so it's worth digging into those feelings with her and proving to her that you're working toward the same goal.

That's a great idea. It is possible. I am the new kid on the block. I will try by being non confrontational. Any specific ideas to how  I can do that? She gets offended easily. I want her to know I am helping.

I'd suggest how much she's helped you since you are in fact the new kid on the block.  And tell her that you want to work with her to have the most efficient partnership possible and use each of your talents to the best of your ability. Then you can lay out how you work best and see where it goes from there.
Thanks! I will try that. You made me feel so much better!
I'm so glad, these can be frustrating situations but sometimes it's worth looking at the other person's perspective.
I agree. Sometimes you just have to take a step back and have a conversation with someone not in the thick of it.
Absolutely, I have no emotional stake in this. The two of you do and that can cloud things sometimes.
I think people get territorial when they have worked somewhere and a new person comes in. I see that now. I am optimistic we will work it out and be a great team!
That's great to hear, I'm glad we were able to chat!
Me too! You really helped me. Have a wonderful day! I know I will since you helped me out.
That's great, good luck!

exactly, I hate to feel that I'm wasting my time

Have you had that conversation with him? I know it might be a difficult conversation to have, but it is often good to get expectations out in the open so you are on the same page with your partner.

Yes, sort of and he gave me the impression that he is not there yet and that was a like almost a year ago, I don't want it to look like I'm pushing him if I try to talk to him again about it. His nonchalant attitude in not seeing the seriousness of it is killing me, I'm just not happy.

no problem, take care.
You as well!
Hey, I just needed someone to talk to and thought of you.
Of course, Amanda. I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
Well, a lot has been happening lately, but something unexpected happened at work today.
Oh? What happened?
Remember the conflict I had with a coworker a while back? They actually apologized today.
That's quite significant! How did that make you feel?
Honestly, it was a relief. We've had tension for months, and their apology felt genuine.
I'm really glad to hear that. A genuine apology can make a big difference in working relationships.

It got me thinking about my aunt's memorial service, too, and how I reconnected with my family then.

That's wonderful. It seems like you're making positive strides in different areas of your life.

A mix of emotions, really. I feel sad and a little lost. But there's also relief, you know? Like, at least now I can move forward instead of being in limbo.
It's understandable to feel conflicted. Breakups can bring about such a wide range of emotions. It's good you're finding some silver lining in it.

It definitely feels overwhelming having to rethink your future plans. Do you feel like talking to your relatives again has given you any support?
Actually, yes. Since I reconnected with my family at my aunt's memorial, they've been really supportive. It's nice to know they're there for me.
That's so important, having a support system to lean on. Have you spoken to any of your friends or coworkers about it?
I told a few friends, and they've been great. Work's been a distraction, and ever since my coworker and I made up, it's been a more positive environment.
It sounds like you're doing a great job surrounding yourself with positive energy and support. What about self-care? Are you finding time for yourself?
I'm trying to. I watched a favorite movie and went for a long walk yesterday to clear my head. It's the little things, I guess.
Definitely, those small acts of self-care can make such a big difference. What do you feel like you need most right now?
I think I just need time to process everything, to let myself feel and heal without rushing into anything new.
Taking the time you need is so important. Give yourself grace, and don't hesitate to reach out if you need someone to talk to.

Hi, I really need to talk about something that's been weighing on me recently.
Of course, Amanda. I'm here for you. What's going on?
I received another negative performance review from my supervisor, and it's really getting to me.
I'm so sorry to hear that. How are you feeling about the review?
It's just so frustrating. I feel like no matter how hard I work, it's never enough.
That's really tough. It sounds like you're putting in so much effort and not getting the recognition you deserve.
Exactly. It's not just this review; it's been a pattern with my supervisor for a while now.
That's understandable. It must be incredibly discouraging to face that repeatedly.
Yes, and it's starting to affect my motivation. I feel so undervalued.
Feeling undervalued at work can be so draining. Do you have any support or allies in the workplace that you can talk to about this?
I've mended things with a coworker recently, which has helped a bit. But it's still so lonely dealing with this.
I'm glad to hear that you have someone you can at least partially lean on. Have you thought about addressing this with anyone higher up or in HR?
I have, but I'm worried it might make things worse with my supervisor if they find out.
That's a valid concern. It's important to weigh the potential outcomes. How are you handling the stress outside of work?
Honestly, not well. The stress is impacting my personal life too, especially after my recent breakup.
It sounds like you're dealing with a lot on your plate all at once. It must be hard to find peace right now.
It is. I'm trying to stay connected with family, but I still feel quite lost.
Reconnecting with family after the memorial service was a positive step. It’s okay to lean on them for support in times like these.
You're right. I need to reach out more, even though it's hard.
Taking that step can be tough, but you have the strength to do it. Remember, you don’t have to go through any of this alone.

Hey Amanda, how are you holding up lately? Anything on your mind?
Hey, I just found out that Bill, my ex, is dating someone new. I didn't think it would affect me so much.

I feel a mix of emotions. On one hand, I know we broke up for good reasons, but on the other, it still hurts seeing him move on so quickly.
It's completely understandable to feel that way. Breakups have a way of stirring up unexpected feelings. Would talking about it more with me help?
Maybe. I'm starting to question if I'm the one who's taking too long to move on. It's like I'm stuck in this limbo.
You're not stuck, you're just processing everything at your own pace. Everyone's journey is different, and it's okay to take the time you need.
I guess. But seeing him happy with someone else makes me doubt myself, like, was I not enough, or did I make the right choice?
Those are hard questions to grapple with. Remember, breaking up was about differences in life goals, not your worth or abilities. You did it for your future.
True, we did have differing goals. I just wish I could turn off the emotional part and focus on that rationality.
Emotions can be really stubborn like that. It's okay to feel and express them, though. They're part of being human and make us whole.
Yeah, I suppose. It's just exhausting at times, especially with everything else going on... like work stress.
I remember you mentioned how undervalued you feel at work. That must amplify everything. How is that going?
Not great. My supervisor is still making things difficult, and I recently got a negative performance review. It's been crushing my confidence.

I thought about it. Maybe seeing a therapist could help, but it's intimidating to take that step.
It's a big step, but it can also be really empowering. Having a space to speak openly and get professional guidance might ease that burden.
You're right. I need to prioritize myself more. It's been hard juggling everything alone.
I'm glad you're considering it. Remember, you're not alone in this. Feel free to reach out whenever you need to talk.
Thanks. It helps knowing there's someone I can lean on. I'll think more seriously about getting support.
That's a great step forward, Amanda. I'm really proud of you for facing all of this and seeking the path that's best for you.
Hello how are you?
I'm, okay, thanks, and you?  I'm feeling a bit down because I'm alone for the holidays.
Well that's no good, does your family live far away?
Yes, my family is scattered all over the country, like Seattle, Georgia, PA.  I'm sure I'm not the only one with no plans this weekend, though.
True but I can understand that, it is hard being alone at the holidays.
Did you have plans this weekend?
No.  My nearby friends all went away for the holidays.  I could probably just occupy my time with things I need or want to do in order to distract myself.
What kind of hobbies do you have?
I'm teaching myself the piano.  I'm also teaching myself  how to work a stenography machine for possible future employment as a stenographer.  I also like to read novels.
I have never understood how those work..I find it amazing someone can type out whole words or sentences with one word
Yeah, it's pretty cool.  For example, if I hit DRAT in one stroke, then "Did there come a time" will appear in English on my machine's  LCD screen.
Wow that is crazy, I don't understand how that works, is it preprogrammed or does it go by how the word sounds?

Each stenographer has their own "Personal Dictionary" which is a list of words in English along with how you in particular write out those words or phrases in steno.  This dictionary is present within the actual steno machine after you transfer it from your laptop to the machine via cable or wifi.  Thus your machine then knows how you write out words in particular and how to translate those words from steno to English - each stenographer writes a little differently.
OK that makes sense, so you basically program it as the user. I take it your stenography machine becomes pretty close to you lol
Is this your first holiday alone?

Yes, exactly!  And it's very important to back up your personal dictionary to the cloud or a seperate drive so that you don't lose it in a hard-drive crash.  A lot of work goes into creating that dictionary!  No, it's happened before, being along for the holidays; but you've helped to cheer me up, so thanks!
No problem, I hope I have made your day a little better!
You have, thanks!  Did you do anything special?
Have a good rest of this year and don't forget to make your New Year's resolution!
I will do that - you too.  Thanks, again...
Not really, stayed home lol... Have a good one!
You too... bye now...
Good day!
What else can I help you with today?

Of course, Amanda. What's been going on?
I had a meeting with my supervisor today and it didn't go as I'd hoped.

Well, I tried to bring up how I've been feeling undervalued and how it's affecting my motivation at work.

Not really... They seemed to dismiss my concerns again, just like last time.
I'm really sorry to hear that, Amanda. It must be so frustrating to feel unheard.
It is. I've been trying so hard to improve things since the negative review, but it feels like nothing I do is ever enough.
You're putting in so much effort, and it's unfortunate that it's not being recognized. How are you holding up emotionally?
Honestly, it feels draining. Sometimes I wonder if I'm just not good enough for this job.
That's such a difficult place to be in. But remember, your worth isn't determined by someone else's recognition or lack thereof.
Thank you for saying that. It helps a little to hear. I just wish things were different at work.
It's completely okay to want things to change. Would it help to focus on small steps towards feeling valued elsewhere, maybe with your coworkers?
Actually, I made amends with a coworker a few months back and our collaboration has improved a lot.
That's great to hear! Having supportive colleagues can make a huge difference. Maybe that's a positive thing to build on?
Yes, it feels nice to have at least one person be supportive. But it's still hard with my supervisor actively undermining my efforts.
I can imagine how exhausting that is. Have you thought about what steps you might want to take next regarding your job situation?
I have thought about looking for a new job, but I'm not sure if I have the energy to go through that process right now.

That's a great approach, Amanda. Remember, you're stronger than you think, and you've already overcome so much.
Thank you so much for listening. It feels a little bit lighter just having someone who understands.
I'm always here for you whenever you need to talk. Don't hesitate to reach out anytime, okay?
I really appreciate that. Let's chat again soon.
Definitely. Take care of yourself, Amanda.
Hey, are you around to chat?

I’ll try to do that. Thanks for listening and helping me sort through this.

Hey, do you have a moment to chat?
